claims.statement: Zoom Platform Studio lets a developer create an API key for Build platform APIs and webhooks; the key is displayed once at creation and cannot be shown again, and a JWT is generated from the account API key and secret.

sources.supports: Create your API Key to access Build platform APIs and webhooks.
This is your new API key. Make sure to copy it before closing this dialog. For security reasons, it will not be shown again.
The JWT is created from your account API key and secret.

claims.statement: Zoom states that the API Key is for server-to-server calls and stays on the backend, that a JWT is for client apps calling Zoom directly and is short-lived and does not expose the secret, and that raw API keys or secrets must never be embedded in client-side code.

sources.supports: **API Key** — Use for server-to-server (S2S) calls. Key stays on your backend.
JWT is short-lived and doesn't expose your secret.
**Never embed raw API keys or secrets in client-side code.**

claims.statement: Zoom documents that a Build platform API key is created with an optional internal name, an expiration of Never, 30 days, 90 days, 180 days or 1 year, an optional IP allowlist and per-product permissions; it can be disabled, re-enabled or revoked (immediately and irreversibly), and its details page shows an ID described as "for internal support", which is a different value from the key.

sources.supports: **Expires after**. Choose an expiration option: Never, 30 days, 90 days, 180 days, 1 year.
**Revoke your key** - Choose to revoke your key. Applications using this key will immediately lose access. This action cannot be undone.
**ID** - The ID, for internal support.

claims.statement: Zoom documents that the JWT generated from the account API key and secret in Platform Studio is given an expiry of 90 minutes, 1 day or 1 week at creation and is copied from a JWT Token field.

sources.supports: Expire in - Choose the time for the key to expire. 90 minutes, 1 day, or 1 week.
Copy your JWT from the **JWT Token** field.

openQuestions.question: Not researched beyond existence: prefix, alphabet, length and any checksum are not stated on the pages read, and no value shape may be inferred from the examples (docs examples are placeholders or illustrative).

The page speaks of an API key and secret; whether the secret is a second credential string, and how the Build-platform JWT relates to Meeting SDK and Video SDK JWTs (documented on other pages not read in this run), is not settled.

Whether the Platform Studio API key is one string or a key and secret pair is unresolved: the Create API Key steps show one dialog with one key shown once, while the same page says the JWT is created from the account API key and secret and the legacy settings page lists an API Key and an API Secret. Which half is the confidential one, and whether the secret is shown once, are not stated for the current flow.

The structure of the Build platform API JWT (algorithm, claims, what it is signed with) is not documented on the pages read; the Video SDK JWT is documented (HS256, signed with the Video SDK secret) but the pages do not say the Build API JWT is built the same way, so no grammar or composition is claimed for it. Whether a JWT held by a client is documented as confidential, as opposed to short-lived and non-exposing of the secret, is not stated.

An Authorization: Bearer value in Build platform requests may be an API Key or a JWT and the pages give no way to tell which from the request alone; only the x-api-key header is documented as API-Key-only. Attribution of a bearer value to the key or to the JWT is therefore not settled.
No prefix, alphabet, length or checksum is stated for the API key, API secret or JWT of the Build platform; examples on the pages are placeholders and no shape is inferred.
